key_insight: PORTER encodes EHR events from language descriptions plus numeric values, avoiding dependence on a fixed event vocabulary while preserving strong predictive performance.
clinical_relevance: This could make foundation models easier to transfer across hospitals and pipelines, reducing the need for manual vocabulary harmonization.
method: Uses a frozen text encoder to represent event descriptions.
Adds a dedicated pathway for numeric values.
Learns patient timeline dynamics with an autoregressively pretrained temporal backbone.
evidence_signal: In 74 pediatric prediction tasks, PORTER matched the fixed-vocabulary model's mean AUROC, recovered 97.1% of target-vocabulary performance on unseen event descriptions, and outperformed the fixed-vocabulary model on MIMIC.
watch_item: Because transfer depends on the quality and consistency of event descriptions and numeric encoding, real-world deployment may still require careful local validation.
paper_title: PORTER: Language-Grounded Event Representations for Portable Structured EHR Foundation Models
